articles.title: Diamond Necklace sparkles in Nassau Stakes
articles.summary: Diamond Necklace enhanced her reputation even further with a dazzling display to make it six from six in the Group One Nassau Stakes on day two of the Glorious Goodwood Festival.
articles.body:
Having rounded off a perfect juvenile campaign with victory in the Prix Marcel Boussac on Arc weekend at ParisLongchamp, Aidan O'Brien's filly has returned to France to secure back-to-back Classic wins this year, in the French 1000 Guineas and French Oaks.

She was the 4-6 favourite to make it six from six as she faced her elders for the first time and while Friendly Soul did her best to shake her off, Ryan Moore always looked ultra-confident in the saddle aboard Diamond Necklace and she pulled two and three-quarter lengths clear with the minimum of fuss.

An impressed Moore said: "That's the best she's felt, she's improving with her racing. Aidan said she was up in her weight a bit today so she's obviously thriving.

"She's classy, it was very easy really. She travelled smoothly and quickened up well, she's a little bit idle in front still, but she's a proper racing machine.

"She gives you a classy feel, every time I've ridden her she's travelled with loads of pace, loads of enthusiasm and she has a turn of foot; that's what her father (St Mark's Basilica) had, a real good turn of foot and that's what's evident with her."

O'Brien was delighted to see Diamond Necklace enhance her unbeaten record and said: "She's lovely and she's progressing and she was heavier today, but Rachel (Richardson, work rider) was confident that was just strength she was building rather than just being heavy and it was the way she went through the line.

"There's a lot of people around her who help her and she's a lovely filly. This was a mile and a quarter against older fillies and we didn't know what was going to happen. We put in a lot of pace as we didn't want a Mickey Mouse race and she has options now.

"You can see her quality the way she travels through a race and Ryan was hoping they would lead him longer and he just had to go on as her stride was getting broken. She is a great cruiser and she has a lot of quality and is progressing great so I'm over the moon."

Diamond Necklace was shortened to 8-1 from 14s for the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe by Paddy Power, but O'Brien is yet to commit on stretching her stamina any further than the 10 furlongs, with the star filly holding a multitude of options for later in the season.

He added: "Constitution River is the boss and everyone has to fall into line behind him. At the moment he is going to York and we're looking forward to that.

"She could stay at a mile and a quarter and go to the race at Leopardstown (Irish Champion Stakes), or France for an Arc trial, she has all those races open to her and she does handle soft ground as well as she handles fast ground.

"The Arc is possibility and she could be a Breeders' Cup filly, it will depend how far we ask her to go. Her next run will tell us where she is going to go and she has a long stride on her and loves nice ground and a fast track, she has a lot of options."

Friendly Soul has endured her fair share of drama since returning from injury this year, being the horse who put a foot in a hole at Haydock before a luckless run in the Duke of Cambridge Stakes at Royal Ascot.

"She's run a fine race against a top class three-year-old who is unbeaten," said Thady Gosden, who trains the five-year-old alongside father John.

"It was a very good effort and we will now in consultation with George and Julia (Strawbridge, owners) look at the programme ahead in which there are some good opportunities for older fillies."

Enceladus impresses in Gordon - but Leger run not set in stone

Joseph O'Brien is keen to keep his options open with Enceladus following his authoritative victory in the Maison Perrier Gordon Stakes at Goodwood.

The Sea The Stars colt has looked much improved since being stepped up in trip this season, with a comeback win at Cork followed by Royal Ascot success in the King George V Stakes.

The William Haggas-trained pair of Desert Hero (2023) and Merchant (2025) won the same Ascot handicap in recent years before landing this Group Three prize and after being sent off a well-backed 6-4 favourite to follow suit, Enceladus finished strongly under Dylan Browne McMonagle, keeping Geryon at bay by a length and a quarter.

Classic sponsors Betfred make Enceladus a 10-1 shot from 25-1 for the Leger, a race which saw O'Brien break his British Classic duck as a trainer with Galileo Chrome six years ago - but the trainer warned he is not certain to head for Doncaster in September.

O'Brien was at Galway rather than Goodwood, from where he told Press Association: "I'm delighted, it was a nice ride from Dylan. It was a really nice performance and he's a progressive, improving colt.

"It was a big step up in class and it's a hard thing to do, but he's going the right way and I'm delighted to have a horse of his potential for Maria and the Niarchos team."

On a Leger bid, he added: "It is one of the more obvious options, but I don't know if we'll rush him past a mile and a half either. Let's see how he pulls up and let the dust settle and we'll lock in his next target after that."

McMonagle said: "He's a lovely, big, straightforward horse. He's done nothing but improve and each run he's getting better.

"I think he's going to be a very nice horse going forward and I do think he's up to that level (Group Twos and Group Ones) with a bit of time.

"As you can see he's still a big baby - when he's getting there he's just doing enough, but he was a good winner.

"He handles that ground well and I think he's got a bit of class - he's a horse to look forward to and one to keep an eye on."

Colin Keane said of the runner-up: "I thought for a few strides that we were going to get to Dylan's horse (Enceladus) but he picked up and went away again.

"I'd say the winner is smart but we're smart as well, he's just a bit of a work in progress. He probably didn't (see it out as well as the winner), but I do think in time he will.

"He's a little hard on himself, he wears earplugs to help him relax so he's a work in progress but a horse with a big future hopefully."

articles.title: Kevin Doyle: Former Premier League striker chasing Cheltenham Festival glory with Augusta Kate and La Bague Au Roi
articles.summary: Reading, Wolves and Republic of Ireland striker Kevin Doyle now runs Slaney River Stud in Wexford, where he has former Grade One-winning mares Augusta Kate and La Bague Au Roi; watch Unbridled On Tour on the At The Races YouTube channel
articles.body:
Since retiring from football, the Republic of Ireland international has been focused on creating the next generation of jumps racing stars, with considerable success already.

Having purchased Grade One-winning mares Augusta Kate and La Bague Au Roi, Doyle's Slaney River Stud has already produced multiple winners.

Doyle's interest in horses and the breeding industry came from his father Paddy, who bred Cheltenham Festival winner Holywell at the family stud. Now, Kevin is hoping he can follow in his father's footsteps.

The Unbridled podcast duo of Matt Chapman and Paddy Brennan are on tour this summer and headed over to Ireland to visit the former Reading and Wolves goalscorer.

"This is what gets me up in the morning now," Doyle explained. "I want a Cheltenham Festival winner now. I've done that [scoring goals]. That's an easy answer.

"Cheltenham is the one you want on the CV. If Holywell was bred here, why not another one?

"You have to hope, horse breeding is just hope. You're doing your best, you have all your routines, but who knows? It's a tough game."

Asked which of his former team-mates he would take with him to Cheltenham for a day out, Doyle added: "John O'Shea. He knows his horses and he'd have the craic and a few pints.

"We were in a syndicate together when we were players and John was the organiser but it wasn't the most successful! The one time a horse we had won, we didn't know it was running!"

Doyle has just over 20 horses on his 40-acre farm, including a Poet's Word colt out of Augusta Kate and recently sold a two-year-old Crystal Ocean gelding out of Augusta Kate to Noel George and Amanda Zetterholm in France.

Dual Grade One winner La Bague Au Roi is also a promising broodmare prospect for Doyle, having survived a freak life-threatening injury at the yard.

"She tripped over her foal, broke her leg and was in hospital for four months. Her chances of surviving the surgery were about five per cent, but she did, she's tough as nails. A normal horse wouldn't be able to come through what she has."

La Bague Au Roi's story very much epitomises the challenging and risky nature of breeding racehorses. But, Doyle does it for the love of the game, not money.

"It costs an awful lot of money to breed horses. I wouldn't be doing it if it was about making money. It's a labour of love.

"Some years you might make some money, but the majority of years you're doing it because you enjoy doing it. There are definitely years where you lose plenty of money.

"Football has allowed me to do this. I wouldn't own Augusta Kate or La Bague Au Roi without it.

"This isn't the most commercial thing in the world and I'm not doing it to make fortunes. You're doing it because you love horses."

Watch Unbridled On Tour in full on the At The Races YouTube channel.

articles.title: American Affair flies the flag for Goldie at Goodwood
articles.summary: American Affair returned to winning ways with a sizzling display in the King George Qatar Stakes on Day Four of Glorious Goodwood, surging to success in the shadows of the post for Jim Goldie and Paul Mulrennan,
articles.body:
Jim Goldie's stable star won the King Charles III Stakes at Royal Ascot last summer, but missed the remainder of the 2025 season through injury.

A second-place finish behind the reopposing Night Raider in Haydock's Temple Stakes in May suggested he retained a good level of his ability, but having trailed home last of all when defending his Ascot title and since come up short in a Listed race at York, he was a 12-1 shot for his latest Group Two assignment.

Always up with the pace in the group that raced closest to the stands rail, American Affair finished off strongly in the hands of his regular partner Paul Mulrennan to get up and beat Rumstar and Time For Sandals down the middle of the track, with Australian raider Asfoora running her best race for a while in fourth.

Goldie senior stayed closer to home, but his son, George, said: "My dad is at Musselburgh, we couldn't both come here, but I think he'll be sorry to have missed out!

"My daughter rides him every day, he's a lovely-natured horse and he's obviously very talented.

"We had faith he'd be back to this level, we've been happy with him at home but things were interrupted by the injury he had at the back end of last year.

"This year it has been a case of building him back up to his best, he showed a glimmer at Haydock three runs ago, but Ascot was a bit of a disaster - he just pulled too hard.

"He ran well at York when he was drawn badly, so we were coming here very hopeful. He's been getting back into that flow of racing properly and finishing his race off.

"We were hoping today was going to suit him better, we were coming here very hopeful."

On future plans, he added: "The plan is to go for the Nunthorpe now, then maybe the Curragh or he could go up to six (furlongs) for the Haydock Sprint Cup.

"We've not entered him in the Abbaye, the Flying Five at the Curragh after the Nunthorpe is more likely."

Weighing-room stalwart Mulrennan said: "He's done everything right today so, touch wood, he comes back from this good. We'll enjoy today, but we've got the Nunthorpe and possibly America would be nice.

"At this stage of the game I've probably got more years behind me than in front of me, but I feel I'm still going strong. It's very competitive, it's hard. I've only got one ride down here this week, but we've made it count.

"I've got my driver with me, Adele (wife). The last time I won it was on Moviesta, Adele drove me then. I've won this race twice and I probably should have won it twice again - Easton Angel probably should have won and Moviesta another year was unlucky, so it's been an unlucky race for me and a lucky race for me, but we got it right today."

Wendy McGrandles of Barraston Racing, who own American Affair with Goldie, said: "He's had one or two excuses and we always felt that he was as good as he was last year. It's once in a lifetime for us, small breeders.

"I remember him as a foal and thinking we could maybe send him eventing if he wasn't fast enough to go racing. He was broken in to go eventing because we weren't sure whether he would be big enough or fast enough to be a racehorse. He can always do that as a second career!"

Burke eyes American trip for Shayem after Thoroughbred success

Karl Burke is eyeing a trip to America with Shayem after he denied the fast-finishing favourite Talk Of New York in the HKJC World Pool Thoroughbred Stakes.

Having finished third behind Wednesday's Sussex Stakes one-two Bow Echo and Gstaad in the St James's Palace at Royal Ascot, this Group Three contest looked a gilt-edged opportunity for Charlie Appleby's Talk Of New York to get back on the winning trail and he was priced up accordingly as the 2-5 market leader.

But while his stablemate Catullus was deployed in a pacemaking role in an attempt to ensure a sound gallop, the favourite was still keen during the early exchanges under William Buick and it then took him a while to find top gear once asked to close the gap.

Karl Burke's Shayem - winner of the Listed Sir Henry Cecil Stakes at Newmarket three weeks ago - was always in the prime position behind Catullus and after grabbing the lead racing inside the final half-furlong, he had enough in hand to keep Talk Of New York at bay by half a length in the hands of Clifford Lee.

"We don't have to lead, but we knew Billy (Loughnane, riding Catullus) was going to go off a nice gallop and Cliff was the only one really to keep tabs on the leader," said Burke.

"Last year, you would have said that he was a soft ground horse but he has proven otherwise this year. We had no qualms about the ground or the track as he handled the undulations at Newmarket well.

"Cliff is very good with his fractions. It was a great performance and Abdulrazaq (Mohamdi, owner) will be delighted as he's a homebred horse as well. He's a great supporter of ours from Dubai.

"There is a nice race at Kentucky Downs for him in September and one at Colonial Downs as well. I don't think they are Grade Ones but they are very valuable races and if if we don't go there, we could come back for the Celebration Mile."

Appleby will let the dust settle on Talk Of New York's disappointing defeat before considering his next move.

He said: "At the top of the hill I thought they'd have to go a bit to go past the lead horse because he's no mug and he likes the track. Stretching to the mile was always going to be the undoing of Catullus - stop the clock a furlong out and we were a comfortable winner.

"William said himself, the front two stole a good march on him and they're two sensible horses. We knew that Catullus was not going to see the mile out eventually but Will said 'I was only just getting rolling there the last furlong'

"I'm not using the track as an excuse, I think the winner is sensible and is improving, he's done everything right, got a nice lead from us and used it, and we've gone and finished the race off.

"You could say do we need to step up in trip? Possibly. But he has got to learn to settle a little bit as well - that first furlong he does want to be a little bit aggressive, but I don't think that was really the undoing of the race to be fair. The pace was on and they weren't coming back at the end of the day."

articles.title: Jockey Jim Crowley announces retirement from the saddle due to injury and plans to start training
articles.summary: Having been on the sidelines since a fall at York last September, top rider Jim Crowley announced his retirement on the final day of the Goodwood Festival with plans to start training in 2027
articles.body:
Crowley began his time in the saddle as a National Hunt jockey but it was not until he switched to the Flat that he really began to showcase his talent.

He rode his first Group-race winner on Rod Millman's Hawridge Prince in the 2006 Jockey Club Cup but had to wait a further five years before a breakthrough at the highest level on Robert Cowell's Prohibit in the King's Stand at Royal Ascot (now King Charles II Stakes).

He became champion jockey in 2016, after which he was appointed as the retained rider for Hamdan Al Maktoum's Shadwell Stud, when his career hit new heights.

Crowley, 48, had the pleasure of riding such champions as Battaash, one of the greatest five-furlong sprinters of the modern era and Baaeed, arguably the best miler since Frankel.

His Shadwell job meant he spent many winters in Dubai where he enjoyed great success, while the likes of Mohaather, Anmaat, Hukum and Ulysses were other top-class horses he will be remembered for.

Unfortunately that day at York has brought his career to a premature end, as following a multitude of operations on his pelvis and legs, he has come to the conclusion that now is the right time for another change of career, as he plans to start training.

Crowley told the Press Association: "I've had an amazing career and to come from jumping and then go on to do as well as I did on the Flat was amazing. I partnered some great horses and it gave me days I could only dream of.

"I never imagined this happening when I came from jumping and I was fortunate to ride all over the world and for some of the best trainers in the world.

"It's been a great career, it's just unfortunate that after my accident at York my body couldn't get back to the level I want to be to race ride again.

"It's nice to announce the retirement at Goodwood. It's my home track and I've had so many good days here and it's nice to finish here."

He went on: "I've always wanted to be a trainer and to train and I think it is the right time for me. It's given me something to get my teeth into. If I could have half as successful training career as I did riding then I would be very happy.

"I've completed my modules and just need to apply for my licence now. I plan on travelling around a bit and spending some time with different trainers and hopefully set up over the winter ahead of next season."

Reflecting on some of his personal highlights from his time in the saddle, it is no surprise Baaeed features heavily.

It is his Queen Elizabeth II Stakes victory at Ascot and then his memorable Juddmonte International romp on his first attempt at 10 furlongs that Crowley remembers most fondly from his time aboard the son of Sea The Stars, thankful to spend the latter stages of his riding career donning the famous Maktoum family silks.

Crowley added: "I've been very privileged and it's thanks to the Maktoum family, Sheikha Hissa and her father who gave me a wonderful opportunity.

"Obviously Baaeed was the best I rode, but there was also Battaash who was by far the best sprinter. There's so many really, Anmaat, Mostahdaf, Hukum who was a great favourite of mine and obviously won the King George, Ulysses, Minzaal - there is so many I've been lucky to ride.

"The day I was made champion jockey was a highlight and so was riding a treble on British Champions Day the day Baaeed beat Palace Pier in the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes.

"Baaeed's Juddmonte Stakes win was another brilliant day, as was Battaash breaking the track record in the Nunthorpe at York."

articles.title: Goodwood: Evening Saigon continues magical week for Wathnan Racing with Stewards' Cup win as Goodie Two Shoes also prevails
articles.summary: Evening Saigon crowned a memorable week at Glorious Goodwood for the Wathnan Racing team when taking out the Saturday feature, the Stewards' Cup in the hands of their number-one rider James Doyle; Goodie Two Shoes won the Qatar Lillie Langtry Stakes
articles.body:
The win was a feather in the cap for the owners, who target this fixture with a vengeance, but perhaps more telling it was a second major handicap of the week for Qatari-born trainer Hamad Al Jehani.

Having also won the Golden Mile with Archivist when Doyle picked the wrong one, Al Jehani was able to celebrate a famous victory with the whole team on this occasion.

Despite higher numbers being preferred at Thursday's draw, the finish was dominated by the eventual winner drawn in 10 beating Stratusnine in five. Jamie Spencer flew from the back on Mitbaahy for third but he was beaten a head and a short head. Completely Random was fourth.

"It's been a great week. Obviously I was very deflated last year with just one and we were really frustrated by that so the memo was we need to do better and that's everyone, including me as well," said Doyle.

"We've done a lot of work this week looking at different tactics and things like that, track position and stuff. All the guys back home in the office, these guys, Hamad has done an unbelievable job with this horse as well.

"He's not an easy conveyance, setting off he was that well in himself he tried to get rid of me the first few strides but that was great.

"We just had the perfect set-up. Dark Thirty was near me, I was able to draft in behind him and we didn't go that mad I didn't think for a Stewards' Cup so I was happy to pull him out before the two and set sail for home.

"I knew the second horse, I won on him the other day at York, he's a pretty decent horse too so it was a good tussle up to the line.

"Hamad and his team, it's nice that they have won the two big handicaps this week."

Al Jehani said: "I am very happy for Evening Saigon and very happy for the team. He performed very well at Royal Ascot and it was the right decision from the management to keep him for the Stewards' Cup.

"It's really important for us and it's a really important race for the season. I'm very happy and thanks to James for giving the horse a great ride.

"It's not easy to be competitive with the best trainers in the world but we try our best and I think we are building in a very good way, with great help from the management. Hopefully, we will improve year by year and we can make Wathnan be in the winner's enclosure more and more."

Wathnan's racing advisor Richard Brown added: "James had a bit of a hard choice but he was pretty firm on riding this lad in the end. Hamad has turned up and won two of the hardest handicaps to win all year. We plot these and work as a team - when these results come off, it's just fantastic for Wathnan and what Wathnan is all about.

"If you look at Hamad's statistics since he started training, they match up with the best trainers in the country. He's a phenomenal horseman and was a very good rider himself. He's very modest about it but he showjumped to a good level. He's a great horseman and he's formed a great team. We all work very closely together and to pull this off is huge for everybody involved."

Goodie Two Shoes sticks her neck out to edge Lillie Langtry battle

Goodie Two Shoes needed to be very brave as she added to Joseph O'Brien and Dylan Browne McMonagle's fantastic week at Goodwood in the Qatar Lillie Langtry Stakes.

With three winners already in the bag, the JP McManus-owned Goodie Two Shoes was sent off an 8/1 chance to bag a first victory of the season but looked to face a tough ask as Santorini Star kicked for home.

She still had ground to make up with 100 yards to the line but the seven-year-old stuck her neck out right where it mattered to get the verdict by a nose.

Goodie Two Shoes was second in the Melbourne Cup in November and a return to Australia will surely now be on the cards following this Group Two triumph.

The winning rider said: "She's a lovely filly, she's improving all the time since she started coming back this year, she's got better with each run.

"I was quietly confident she would get a lot closer to these fillies, she ran well last year [third] when the ground turned up soft but she would gallop down the road for you, she handles quick ground. I got a lovely split through them and she wanted to win.

"To be honest I didn't think I'd won but I looked back at the camera and she had her head stuck down for me at the right time; I did think Tom (Marquand) had won but we came out the right side of it.

"These are very, very special silks to put on. A big thanks to JP for putting me up and she's going to have a nice campaign through to the end of the season.

"I'm sure the Melbourne Cup is probably the main target, the boys will know that and Joseph and JP will discuss it but I'd probably guess that's the obvious target."

Sir Anthony McCoy, representing McManus, said: "I didn't think she had won but Jason Weaver said right on the nod, not before the line or after the line but right on the line, she put her head in the right place.

"She got a good ride - he was going to ride her for that bit of luck, down the inside, and he got a lot of luck. When you are as good as Dylan Browne McMonagle and you are riding for Joseph O'Brien, you seem to get a lot of luck.

"Dylan was over at mine a few times when he was 11 or 12. He is very mechanically correct, like Ryan Moore, and he's got that chip - that little thing where he could go the wrong way. I mean it in a good way. As Frankie found out one day at Ascot, he has that little edge to him.

"She was second in a Melbourne Cup and I thought she had been quite well handicapped for the Galway Plate if she ran there off 123. It's nice when you win races like this and hopefully she will be able to go back to the Melbourne Cup."

articles.title: Prix Rothschild: Blue Bolt confirms superiority over Precise in Deauville Group 1
articles.summary: Having been manoeuvred towards the stands-side rail by Colin Keane, Blue Bolt dug deep to deny Precise again in the Group 1 Prix Rothschild at Deauville.
articles.body:
Runner-up to Fallen Angel in the Sun Chariot at Newmarket at the end of last season, Andrew Balding's filly has taken her game to another level this term with a comeback win in Listed company at Goodwood followed by big-race triumphs in the Duke of Cambridge Stakes at Royal Ascot and the Falmouth at Newmarket.

The four-year-old was renewing rivalry with the July course runner-up, Aidan O'Brien's Irish 1,000 Guineas and Coronation Stakes heroine Precise, and at one stage it looked like the latter may take her revenge in the hands of Ryan Moore.

But Blue Bolt was doing her best work at the finish under Colin Keane and lunged late to claim a seventh win from 10 career starts, with Sir Mark Prescott's Coronation Stakes fourth Moon Target bettering that result with a fine effort to finish third.

Balding told Sky Sports Racing: "She's some filly, she really is - and Colin gave her a wonderful ride. It wasn't very comfortable watching it, I thought we were beat in the last furlong, but he's judged it to perfection.

"She's got great physical strength for a filly, that's her biggest quality, and she's got great desire as well. A big thank you to the team at home and Alfie Redman who rides her every day. She's not easy and likes to take control of things, but he's really mastered her this last six months and done a great job of it.

"She likes to get on with it, she's a powerful traveller and knows her strength, so it's about harnessing that in the right direction."

Blue Bolt now looks set to bid for further Group One success in Ireland, with her trainer adding: "The great thing about her is she's effective on any ground, which is a big help.

"We always felt the Matron Stakes at Leopardstown (September 12) was her race this year and we won't lose sight of that for anything prior to that."

articles.title: Shergar Cup: Jamie Lynch's five horses to follow at Ascot on Saturday as international stars battle it out
articles.summary: Sky Sports Racing's senior form analyst Jamie Lynch nominates five runners to note at the Shergar Cup from Ascot on Saturday, all six races are live on Sky Sports Racing; Ryan Moore returns to the team competition for the first time since 2006
articles.body:
1.35 - Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Dash (5f)

A fortnight ago at Cork, KENDALL ROY was beaten a short head and a neck in a five-furlong handicap which was sub-57 seconds, and he felt the pinch of that before finishing off strongly, so much so that he could be considered rather lucky to be left on the same mark.

His trainer Kate McGivern is three from nine at home in Ireland this year, and she clearly has a touch with sprinters given Grayrobin's rapid rise. With All Ways Glamorous, Gold Star Hero and Cinque Verde in direct competition, the Dash projects to get very hot very quickly, which will be right up Kendall Roy's fast-finishing street.

2:10 - Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Stayers (2m)

Mark Johnston was beaten a short head into second with Spirit of Love in the very first Shergar Cup Stayers event and, a quarter of a century on, the same stable, with Charlie in charge, is still fashioning the same sort.

POLE STAR needs a bounce back, but returning to two miles will help him no end and he's now lower in the handicap than when he won a Racing League race around this time last year.

He maps to be prominent in a race without much pace and, interlinked, he has the acute advantage of Dylan Browne McMonagle, whose stats this season are all the more striking at staying trips, with a 20 per cent strike-rate in Britain and Ireland.

3:20 - Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Sprint (6f)

The 2025 Windsor Castle winner HAVANA HURRICANE has only recently dipped down to handicaps, after contesting the Commonwealth Cup, but they've both been over five furlongs, which no longer gets to the bottom of him.

But, he generated the flame symbol for his finish at Sandown and was beaten only two-and-a-half lengths - again after good late work - in a better handicap than this at Ascot last time in which the first two were Dubai Bling and Behike.

The seduction of a straight six means this race, more than any at the Shergar Cup, traditionally goes the way of the hold-up horses (the last six winners have all come from the back of the field), and Havana Hurricane certainly fits that bill.

3:55 - Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Classic (1m 4f)

HOSEKI recorded closing splits of 11.9s, 11.3s and 11.5s - rare indeed for this course and distance - when she overcame a steady gallop last month, probably undersold by a 5lb rise.

The other upshot of the pedestrian pace that day is we're still to see much of the stamina that Hoseki is bred for (from the family of Al Aasy and Align The Stars).

She's on a roll, as is her rider Saffie Osborne, and, for many, Hoseki is the make-or-break horse of the 2026 Shergar Cup. I think she'll make it four in a row.

4:30 - Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Mile (1m)

At the age of five, 31 races into his career, TWO TRIBES will be trying a mile for the first time here, but his finishing speed and run-out speed from the seven-furlong International - in which he was second (of 16) to Amazing Journey - raises hope for the requisite stamina.

It's easy to hand him a pass for last week when favourite to make it back-to-back Stewards' Cups, as he all but came down leaving the stalls, and, given his gears and late-coming style, the race flow of a round mile at Ascot may just suit him, plus he has McMonagle on board.

articles.title: Hollie Doyle: Expect Thunder Call to play a part in Shergar Cup at Ascot live on Sky Sports Racing on Saturday
articles.summary: Our ambassador Hollie Doyle gives her verdict on the Ascot card with the Shergar Cup taking centre stage on Saturday with Ryan Moore, Christophe Lemaire and Yutaka Take all in action; watch all six races live on Sky Sports Racing
articles.body:
Glamorous can have them singing in the Valleys

It's exciting for Welsh trainer Chris Mason to have a runner in this year's Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup and they'll be singing loud in his Monmouth village on Saturday night if All Ways Glamorous takes the opening Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Dash (1.35) at Ascot.

His five-year-old, who will be representing Team Europe, already has a course-and-distance win to his name after impressing off a five-pound lower rating two weeks ago and can give French rider Marie Velon a great experience.

Europe's Bolo Neighs looks poised to get his head in front soon after flashing home in the same race last time but has work to do to turn the tables, while Ryan Moore can be relied upon to get the best out of my old friend Spartan Arrow who has been working well enough to put points on the board for Great Britain and Ireland.

Shrimp Shady is a young horse going places and can give Great Britain and Ireland maximum points in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Stayers (2.10).

Andrew Balding's four-year-old has landed big marathon handicaps at Chester and Newbury already this summer and looks made for this stiff two-mile trip with Ryan Moore set for another plum ride.

Europe, who haven't won the Shergar Cup since back-to-back triumphs in 2013 and 2014, are also well represented with the Ian Williams-trained Hermetic likely to build on his fourth at Newcastle under the classy Christophe Lemaire. This ex-French winner could be well treated off a mark of 81.

It was good to see Richard and Peter Fahey come off the cold list at Southwell on Thursday, just in time for Castle Stuart's run in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Challenge (2.45).

Hong Kong, who are competing as a team for the first time, have a live contender in this reliable four-year-old who has been unfortunate to bump into two Roger Varian improvers at York this summer. South African Luke Ferraris, a well-known name in China, can be relied upon to get the best out of him.

Ian Williams has the services of Irish champion Dylan Browne McMonagle on his likely favourite Night Breeze , a consistent sort who was a good third at Goodwood but needs a career best to win this, which could make him a shade vulnerable. Insanity took this two years ago for Rachel King and can go well again under Europe's Velon.

Thunder a big player for Hong Kong debutant

Thunder Call didn't appear to enjoy Newmarket's undulations last time but can get back to winning ways for the Hong Kong team in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Sprint (3.20).

William Haggas' sprinter won in the style of a very nice horse at York before that and promises to be ideally suited to the stiff finish at Ascot, with British racing debutant Jerry Chau on board.

One to watch out for is Great Britain and Ireland's Cape Ashizuri who is unexposed enough to put a disappointing run in a big field last time behind him. John and Sean Quinn will be happy to have McMonagle in the plate.

Newmarket-based Italian trainer Marco Botti can put maximum points on the scoreboard for Great Britain and Ireland in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Classic (3.55).

Archers Bay , another strong chance for Moore, has been bumping into the likes of Ancient Egypt and Heraldry since winning at Newmarket - form that stands out in what doesn't look the strongest renewal.

Team-mate Hoseki is on a roll after rattling up a hat-trick in a course-and-distance fillies' race under a light weight. I'm not sure how much improvement she has left off this five-pound higher mark, though. A more interesting proposition could be Jessie Harrington's Pierre Grosse who is still a maiden but brings solid form to the race in first-time cheekpieces.

The closing Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Mile (4.30) could determine where the trophy goes this year with Europe's Bullet Point the one I expect to capitalise.

Lemaire partners Haggas' gelding, who has the sheepskins on for the first time after not hitting top stride in two starts this year. He is only a pound higher than when he won a big handicap at York's Ebor Festival 12 months ago.

I also like Rest of the World's Ebt's Guard , a course-and-distance winner who has run well in big handicaps at Royal Ascot and Sandown and looks a big player for Indian ace Suraj Narredu, who won the competition with Team Asia last year.

The Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup has given me some of my most special days on a racecourse and I'm excited to watch the action unfold in front of what will once again be a big, enthusiastic crowd at Ascot.

I've been lucky enough to ride three winners in the competition including a double three years ago when I was presented with the Alistair Haggis Silver Saddle Trophy for the highest points scorer.

I was on the winning team in 2023 and 2018 and can tell you that lifting that cup is such a buzz. Being part of a team competition is something we don't often experience as jockeys so the rivalry out on the turf on Saturday will be intense.

articles.title: Weekend Winners: Kate Tracey, Sam Boswell and Jamie Lynch have their say on Saturday's Shergar Cup Sprint at Ascot
articles.summary: Ahead of another fun-filled Saturday with a typically competitive edition of the Shergar Cup at Ascot, the Weekend Winners team discuss their best bets for the Sprint; watch all six races from Ascot live on Sky Sports Racing
articles.body:
Thunder Call heads the market for this typically competitive heat having gone down on his sword when looking to complete a hat-trick in a hot three-year-old handicap at Newmarket last time out, but all three of our panellists are taking on the William Haggas-trained sprinter.

"Quick conditions will help for Havana Hurricane, trained by Eve Johnson Houghton. He's up to six furlongs from five last time and this is only his third handicap start too. He was well liked last year and won the Windsor Castle.

"The key here is up in trip and being held up. The last five winners of this race have come from off the pace as they go a fair gallop. There is a lot to like with him here and he's a proper each-way price."

"The horse for me is Figjam , who was second at Doncaster last season in a competitive handicap. She had been pitched into the deep end in the Firth Of Clyde and ran fourth. She makes her handicap debut.

"Her rating could be a little high but the thing with her is she's still so unexposed for a trainer who has done well with sprinting mares this season in Katie Scott. I think she's a lot more unexposed than these and has a good chance here."

"I'm going against the favourite with the John and Sean Quinn-trained Cape Ashizuri who has been chucked into the deep end on a few occasions. He ran in the Champagne Stakes on his second start where he did finish last, but they thought enough of him to pitch him into a Group Two on his second start. He then bumped into Saber Strike who is a good horse in his own right, before flopping at York in a big-field handicap.

"That was only his fifth career start and I'm willing to put a line through it, and he's got Dylan Browne McMonagle jocked up for the first time who is one of the best in the Shergar Cup. The ground should be fine for him and he's a good bet."

articles.title: Big Buck's: Paul Nicholls pays tribute as legendary stayer dies aged 23
articles.summary: Paul Nicholls has paid tribute to his "invincible" hurdler Big Buck's, who has passed away at the age of 23; The Ditcheat horse, owned by the late Andy Stewart, won four consecutive Stayers' Hurdle crowns from 2009 to 2012.
articles.body:
Owned by the late Andy Stewart, he was part of a golden age for trainer Paul Nicholls as he counted Kauto Star, Denman, Master Minded and Neptune Collonges among his stablemates.

Big Buck's had always been viewed by connections as a potential top-class chaser, however, a fall at the final fence in the 2008 Hennessy Gold Cup saw him revert back to hurdles and he never looked back.

He won what is now the Stayers' Hurdle a record four times, the Liverpool Hurdle four times and three times he came home in front in the Long Walk Hurdle.

Big Buck's, who struck up a great relationship with Ruby Walsh, was a fan favourite as he would often hit a flat spot in his races before powering to victory.

Nicholls told the Press Association: "Ability-wise he was probably as good as anything I've ever trained, it's just a shame he couldn't jump a chase fence.

"He was a wonderful horse for a wonderful owner who deserved to own a great horse like that. Andy enjoyed the whole journey and shared it with everybody.

"The horse had a brilliant life and had a great time with us and then a great time with Mike and Lucy Felton in retirement, but sadly time caught up with him.

"I was very lucky to have him at the same time as Kauto Star, Neptune Collonges, Master Minded and Denman. He was definitely as good as any of them."

One of the last surviving members of that halcyon period for the Ditcheat handler, Big Buck's would go on to pass Sir Ken and win a then record 18 straight National Hunt races when reverting to hurdles, an achievement only eclipsed by Altior since.

However, for Nicholls there will always be the question of how high he could have climbed if remaining over the larger obstacles.

"He won the Graded race at Aintree over fences, jumped 18 fences and jumped them 18 different ways and still won," said Nicholls.

"It made me think he was a certainty in the Hennessy and he was unlucky that day, but he just wasn't a natural jumper of a fence.

"If Kauto Star hadn't been about at that time then we probably would persevered over fences and he had the ability to win a Gold Cup. If he had won the Hennessy that day it would have definitely given us a headache and it would have been interesting where he would have ended up.

"But over hurdles he was invincible. Andy said I was bonkers, but going back over hurdles was the best thing we ever did. History tells you how good he was and Cheltenham, Aintree, Newbury, Ascot - if there was a big staying hurdle race, he won them all - all those Grade Ones on the trot, what a horse."

Big Bucks would become a standing dish on Thursdays at the Cheltenham Festival, with his famous flat spot often sparking nervous gasps from supporters before hitting top gear and surging up the Cheltenham hill under Walsh.

When asked to nominate just one race in Big Bucks' decorated career littered with so many great triumphs it was his fourth-straight success in the day three feature, when seeing off arguably the deepest field he met, edging out Irish raider Voler La Vedette, that Nicholls remembers most fondly.

"His fourth World Hurdle was the one that sticks out as being very special," said Nicholls.

"But we had so many great days with such a brilliant horse and we were all very lucky to be associated with him."

articles.title: Shergar Cup: Ryan Moore helps Great Britain and Ireland to Ascot crown
articles.summary: Alongside team-mates Saffie Osborne and Dylan Browne McMonagle, Ryan Moore produced two inspired rides to clinch the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup, as well as the prestigious SIlver Saddle Trophy for himself at Ascot; Having won the first two races, Team Hong Kong finished second.
articles.body:
Winner of the Silver Saddle on his last appearance at the team-based meeting in 2006, Moore has usually been required to ride on a Group One card in Ireland.

But with that meeting put back 24 hours he was free to attend and delighted the Ascot crowd.

Team Great Britain and Ireland topped the standings on 81 points from Team Hong Kong in second on 62, with Moore's individual haul of 47 enough to take the Silver Saddle.

He first struck on Dylan Cunha's Asgard's Captain (13-2) who stuck to his task gamely to win the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Challenge by a length and a quarter from Yutake Take on Sportingsilvermine for the Rest of the World.

Moore said: "Dylan did say he could be a little bit lazy, but he has an uncomplicated attitude and to just help him through it and it was straightforward, really.

"It's great to get Dylan a winner here today and the owners will be delighted as they were all looking forward to it, so it's a good job the horse has performed today."

In the penultimate Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Classic, he gave Marco Botti's Archers Bay (5-2) a textbook ride coming home three-and-a-quarter lengths clear of Christophe Lemaire on King Of Berkshire for Team Europe.

Having run in the Italian Derby earlier in the season, he looked the class act and so it proved.

In the closing Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Mile, Moore finished third on Ozat behind the Frida Valle Skar-ridden Crown Board (10-1), but her Team Europe were not in contention for top honours by then.

Saffie Osborne thrives in the team environment and got her name on the scoresheet when Tim Easterby's Red Spells Danger justified 2-1 favouritism in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Sprint.

Osborne was leading rider in the Racing League on three occasions and is captaining Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle in Team Great Britain and Ireland.

She said: "I heard a few people knocking this horse today but I thought the track would really suit and it has. I'm just glad I pulled my finger out.

"Looking at the standard of jockeys here today, it's amazing - look at our team with Ryan Moore and Ireland's champion jockey.

"The win for me today is that I made Ryan laugh a couple of times, so I'm quite happy with that!"

Team Hong Kong had earlier set the pace winning the first two races.

Jerry Chau gave them the perfect start when partnering Tuco Salamanca to a clear-cut victory in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Dash.

Representing a team making its Shergar Cup debut, Chau, 26, gave Ollie Sangster's four-year-old the perfect ride, taking a lead into the final furlong before a gap opened up seamlessly.

Tuco Salamanca (4-1) quickened impressively to beat Gold Star Hero, ridden by Chau's team-mate Vincent Ho, by a length and a half.

Fandom and Suraj Narredu were third for the Rest of the World.

Chau told Sky Sports Racing : "It felt amazing when I hit the line.

"No words can describe riding a winner at Ascot. I grew up watching Ryan Moore on YouTube. I watched him as much as I could."

Luke Ferraris did not have to wait long to play his part for Team Hong Kong as after an opening race one-two from his team-mates, he drove home Dancing In Paris to win the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Stayers.

Riding the Ian Williams-trained 17-2 shot, Ferraris came with a late run to collar Moore on Andrew Balding's Shrimp Shady to win by a length.

Mountain Road was third for Yutake Take and the Rest of the World.

Ferraris said: "That's phenomenal, he's a lot fitter than me! He was turned out in great order.

"He didn't settle as good as he should have, but he still produced a great turn of foot.

"I think I've only ridden in one two-mile race in recent years, so it was a bit of a change.

"We've a good group of young riders representing Hong Kong, so let's hope it continues."

articles.title: British MotoGP: Raul Fernandez dominates at Silverstone to beat Martin
articles.summary: Aprilia rider’s victory over Jorge Martin extends Silverstone’s run of different Grand Prix winners to twelve in a row.
articles.body:
Trackhouse Aprilia Racing’s Raul Fernandez led from the opening lap to win the British MotoGP at Silverstone on Sunday, capitalising on an early setback for championship leader Jorge Martin.

Fernandez swept past pole-sitter Martin into turn one and never looked back, stretching his advantage to more than four seconds before taking the chequered flag 2.54 seconds clear. The victory was the Spaniard’s second in MotoGP and his first since last year’s Australian Grand Prix, completing an impressive recovery from a crash in Saturday’s sprint.

list 3 of 4 Morocco, Algeria book World Cup 2027 spots with quarterfinal wins at WAFCON

list 4 of 4 Tennis: World number one Sabalenka ousted in Toronto by Alexandrova

“I am really happy for the team. Yesterday (Saturday) I was quite frustrated after my mistake. But we are human and it is part of the sport,” Fernandez said.

Spain’s Martin, who won the sprint, was hampered at the start when his ride-height device failed to disengage at turn one, dropping him behind Marc Marquez and fellow Aprilia rider Marco Bezzecchi. The championship leader recovered to reclaim second from Bezzecchi on lap nine but was unable to get close enough to challenge Fernandez.

Martin’s runner-up finish extended his championship lead to 31 points, with Bezzecchi, who finished third, moving up to second in the standings. Ogura lost ground after his first retirement of the season, falling 37 points behind Martin.

“The results here are a big boost of confidence for me and the team,” Martin said.

“It seems like we found a bit of direction to get the momentum on our side now. The race was fantastic. I made a small mistake at the start, but I am glad I was able to fight back.”

Defending world champion Marc Marquez endured another difficult afternoon, finishing seventh after starting sixth on the grid and dropping to fourth in the standings.

Bezzecchi faced stiff competition from Gresini Racing’s Alex Marquez, who made a late mistake and dropped back. Alex Marquez continued to put pressure on Bezzecchi, but was unable to chase him down as the Aprilia rider finished third to secure his second podium of the weekend.

The result was particularly significant for Bezzecchi, who led the MotoGP championship earlier this season and was recording his first Sunday finish since winning his home Italian Grand Prix at the end of May.

Alex Marquez came fourth, KTM’s Pedro Acosta fifth and VR46 Racing’s Fabio Di Giannantonio sixth.

articles.title: 'Exciting' Sun Goddess looks the part for record-breaking Aidan O'Brien in Phoenix Stakes at the Curragh
articles.summary: Aidan O'Brien enhanced his record-breaking tally in the Phoenix Stakes to 18 on Sunday as his 'very special' filly Sun Goddess gained a first success at the top level in the hands of Ryan Moore.
articles.body:
Johannesburg (2001), George Washington (2005), Holy Roman Emperor (2006) and Caravaggio (2016) are just a few of the big names to have won this Group One prize over the years and Sun Goddess was the 5-4 favourite to add to that tally under Ryan Moore.

The daughter of Sioux Nation - who also won this race for the same connections in 2017 - had won each of her two previous starts over the course and distance, including a Group Two on her latest outing, with a runner-up finish behind George Boughey's Libertango in the Albany Stakes at Royal Ascot sandwiched in between.

With stablemate Carry The Flag setting a furious early pace, Moore was content to bide his time aboard Sun Goddess, but she came through stylishly on the far side of the track, racing inside the final two furlongs and was well on top as she passed the post a length and a quarter clear of Folsom Blues.

O'Brien said: "She's a beautiful filly. She ran well at Naas the first day then came back here to win her maiden and then she went to Ascot probably a little under par, with the benefit of hindsight.

"Then she came back here a week after and won even though she was in Ascot the week before. She's obviously very special and everything went really well since Ascot."

He added: "She has a lot of gears and a very high cruising pace. Ryan said they went fast and he just said when he started to ask her she motored clear. He said she'll have no problem getting seven furlongs. She's very exciting."

Big Mojo bounces back to winning ways at the Curragh

Big Mojo made the most of having his sights lowered with victory in the FBD Hotels And Resorts Phoenix Sprint Stakes at the Curragh.

Mick Appleby's colt showed his worth at the highest level last season, winning the Sprint Cup at Haydock as well as finishing a neck second to No Half Measures in the July Cup at Newmarket.

The four-year-old has struggled so far this year, finishing down the field at York, Royal Ascot and on his second attempt at July Cup glory last month, but he had less on his plate in Ireland and stamped his class with a one-and-a-quarter-length verdict over Bucanero Fuerte under Tom Marquand.

A return to Haydock looks to be on the agenda, as does the Breeders' Cup, and Appleby, saddling his first winner on Irish soil, said of the 5-4 favourite: "He's done it well. We brought him here just to give him a bit more confidence, really. I think he was just lacking a bit in confidence with the big races he's run in.

"Now that he's got his head back in front hopefully he'll go and do it again. He's as good as ever. He's just got a bit more laid-back, like me! It's hard to win these races.

"There are a lot of good sprinters about. He's done it well enough. He only did what he wanted to do. There's a lot more there."

Michael O'Callaghan is confident Push The Boat Out can make his mark at a higher level following his successful debut in the Follow Us On Instagram @ GuidenstownStud Irish EBF Maiden.

Although not that well fancied in the market at 16-1, the Kodi Bear colt quickened smartly to record a comfortable victory under Colin Keane and it came as no surprise to his trainer.

O'Callaghan said: "He's a horse we've held in high regard from the moment we got him, but saying that I did have him slightly undercooked because he's very natural at home.

"He jumped and travelled with a lot of natural pace and quickened up well. Colin was quite taken by him and said he should have no problem stepping up into stakes company.

"I don't think he'll have any problem going another furlong and I think he could be a high-class stakes horse. We'll see how he is in the morning and see what there is between now and the National Stakes and go from there."

Aidan O'Brien's Ibelieveicanfly (13-8 favourite) opened her account at the fourth attempt in the Grand Hotel Malahide Irish EBF Fillies Juvenile Race.

Fourth, second and fourth in her first three races, the daughter of Frankel was fitted with a hood for her latest assignment and came good in some style, rewarding her supporters with a dominant five-length win in the hands of Ryan Moore.

"The better the race, the better she is going to be - she has such a high cruising pace," said O'Brien.

"In an ordinary run maiden, she is just in a gear too high. She has a lot of class. There was plenty of pace on and Ryan was very happy with her."

O'Brien and Moore doubled up in the Guidenstown Stud Irish European Breeders Fund Maiden with 8-15 favourite Shakespeare.

The son of Dubawi had shown a good level of ability with placed efforts on his first two starts and duly made it third time lucky without too much fuss.

O'Brien added: "He's a lovely big horse who does everything right. He's a little bit of a baby. That's why it took two runs for him to get to where he is.

"He's still not there. He has a lot of ability and is in the 'could be anything' category, really.

"Size, power, quality, speed, stamina - he has everything. Hopefully he's going to be something to look forward to."

articles.title: Samangan stars in Prix Maurice de Gheest
articles.summary: Francis-Henri Graffard took the headlines again in Deauville as the Aga Khan Studs-owned Samangan gained a first success at the top level in the Prix Maurice de Gheest.
articles.body:
Always close to the pace-setting Afandy over the intermediate six-and-a-half-furlong trip, the Aga Khan Studs-owned Samangan battled through the final quarter-mile to master Stolen Kiss and just found the post coming in time to foil the William Haggas-trained Division, who flashed home under James Doyle.

The winner had been fourth in the Prix Jean Prat last time out in which True Love was second, but comprehensively reversed form with the Ballydoyle Classic heroine on this occasion.

Nemone Routh, racing manager for the owners in France, told Sky Sports Racing: "He's a lovely horse, he's very genuine. He was always going to follow Afandy and then he was really brave.

"He could (go to Ascot on Champions Day), but I think he's better on good, firm ground, that's another thing we've found this year. I think if it got too soft he wouldn't go there. He's a relaxed horse and he can get seven (furlongs). It all depends on the ground."

Graffard added: "I am very pleased for the stable. He is a colt we have always held in high regard. Things did not go as planned at the beginning of the season, but he also needed to gain experience.

"His previous races have toughened him up and this victory is the result of the experience he has been able to acquire.

"His next target could be the Qatar Prix de la Foret, provided the ground is not too testing for him. He is a Group One winner and exceptionally well bred, so he has earned his place at stud as a stallion. My job is done!"

Distant Storm boosted star three-year-old milers Bow Echo and Gstaad as he made a winning reappearance in the Prix Daphnis.

Third to Bow Echo in the 2000 Guineas at Newmarket before finding only Gstaad too good in the Irish equivalent, Charlie Appleby's colt had been off since that run at the Curragh.

Returning to the track in Group Three company, Billy Loughnane's mount was a little tight for room before getting out to give chase to well-backed Italian raider Grand Son Of Dark.

The Godolphin runner had a fair bit to do but always gave the impression he would get there and he duly did, to set up a return to bigger and better things.

Loughnane said: "I ended up a little further back than ideal, but the pace was even which was ideal and when I popped him out the top of the straight he had a target to run at.

"He's a horse that doesn't do too much when he's there, so having a horse to aim at was good and he won cosily in the end. He's horse that has a nice turn of foot, he takes a bit of time to pick up but when he does he's electric through the line.

"I was pretty confident I had everything covered."

articles.title: Bow Echo: George Boughey's unbeaten star miler in shock retirement from racing after setback
articles.summary: Bow Echo retires a perfect six from six, winning three Group One races this season, earning him comparisons with the great Frankel; George Boughey has called it "the honour of a lifetime" to train Bow Echo
articles.body:
Having won the 2000 Guineas, the St James's Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot and the Sussex Stakes this season, Bow Echo was being lined up for Sunday's Prix Jacques le Marois.

Announcing the surprise news on his X account, Boughey said: "It is with great disappointment that we have to announce that Bow Echo has had a setback and will be retired from racing.

"It has been the honour of a lifetime to train a horse like Bow Echo. He has given us some extraordinary days and taken everyone involved on a journey we will never forget.

"To retire unbeaten, having won the 2000 Guineas, St James's Palace Stakes and Sussex Stakes says everything about what an exceptional racehorse he has been.

"Bow Echo's remarkable story began with his owner-breeder, the late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid and it is a great sadness that he was not here to see what a lifetime of breeding was able to produce.

"Bow Echo's unbelievable constitution and extraordinary ability have set him apart. We will all miss seeing him at home and on the racecourse but we are incredibly excited for his next chapter and in time, to see a new generation of his progeny on the racecourse."

articles.title: Hollie Doyle: Clive Cox can take out the Newbury feature with talented-colt Coppull
articles.summary: Our ambassador Hollie Doyle gives her verdict on the action from Newbury and Ripon, providing her take on the Hungerford Stakes and Great St Wilfrid.
articles.body:
Extra furlong ideal for Hungerford fancy

Coppull showed me enough in the Group One July Cup to convince me he is up to taking the Visit Malta Hungerford Stakes (3.10) at Newbury on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Racing.

Clive Cox's three-year-old took a long time to get organised at Newmarket where the winner - Comanche Brave - got first run but this strong traveller should enjoy the extra furlong on a more conventional track.

Never So Brave will have his supporters on the back of his second in the Criterion at York over this seven-furlong trip but is struggling to get his head in front this season while Godolphin's Symbol Of Honour is solid but has never won over this distance.

A more interesting runner for me is William Haggas's Extremely Zain , a course and distance winner who ran better than his final placing suggests in the International at Ascot and remains on an upward curve. This is a step up in grade, but he can acquit himself well in an ordinary renewal.

Millionaire sets standard in Geoffrey Freer

Dubai Honour , who has four Group Ones and over £5 million in prize money on his CV, can roll back the years in the opening Highclere Thoroughbred Racing Geoffrey Freer Stakes (1.25) at Newbury.

This eight-year-old has given my husband Tom (Marquand) some of his finest moments in the saddle and, with an excellent record fresh, can make it win number 11 on his return from a summer break.

There is little between Mount Atlas and Tabletalk on their efforts in the Silver Cup at York, but I can't see either finding the improvement needed to lower the colours of Dubai Honour on these terms.

Gamrai went down fighting in the Copper Horse at Royal Ascot and, whilst he's in deeper waters now, may just benefit from the change of scenery, having joined George Scott from John and Thady Gosden.

Now he has got his head back in front, Richard Hannon's Wheels Of Fire can put up another bold show in the D&H, Excellence In Nutrition Handicap (1.55) at Newbury.

He beat the re-opposing Hypnotised comfortably at Sandown and a six-pound rise may not be enough to stop him following up under Pat Dobbs, even though that rival is better off at the weights.

Chris Mason's Glamorous Breeze is entitled to go close on her solid performance at Goodwood, but Kinswoman has come up short in Listed and Group company and still has something to prove, even though she's dropping back into a handicap off a reduced rating.

Humam's front-running third in a warm race at Newmarket puts him bang there for the TPT Fire Handicap (2.35) at Newbury. I loved the way this former Andrew Balding runner stuck to the task to register his best effort for Stuart Williams since being gelded in the winter.

Racing off an unchanged mark, his most recent form is more compelling than that of market rival Scoville , who has disappointed in both the Royal Hunt Cup and the Golden Mile at Goodwood and needs to improve for this drop in trip.

Eve Johnson Houghton's admirable Great Acclaim has been running well in big races such as the Victoria Cup and Buckingham Palace but needs some respite from the handicapper.

Malton trainer Nigel Tinkler and his apprentice Alex Jary have a great chance of pulling off a memorable big race double at Ripon on Saturday, starting with Lord Roxby in the William Hill/MND Association Great St Wilfrid Handicap (3.25).

Middleham Park's four-year-old returns to the North Yorkshire track in top form after beating fancied rival Dark Cloud Rising over course and distance at the start of the month. He also put a big field to the sword at York earlier this summer and can cope with a five-pound rise against some smart rivals who have a bit more to prove.

Likely favourite Fast Track Harry put in an improved performance in first-time cheekpieces at Ascot last time but I'm not convinced the track will suit while the class horse in the race, Aramram , must overcome a low draw and he ran badly from a similar position in this race two years ago.

In the consolation race, the William Hill Supporting MND Silver Cup Handicap (2.55), Nigel runs Magic Boy who ticks plenty of boxes in a wide open, big field dash.

This four-year-old is less exposed than most and showed his potential with a hard-fought win against 18 rivals at York last month before a slow start compromised his chances back there three weeks ago.

Magic Boy is ideally drawn in stall 14 and has previous track form which is always so important at the Garden Racecourse. He has finished second on both his visits but can go one better despite needing a career best.

Another interesting contender is Clive Cox's Mythical Composer who is also potentially well-drawn in stall 15 but needs to bounce back from a poor effort at Goodwood, his first since being gelded.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft .

articles.title: Weekend Winners: Rayif fancied to take Prix Jacques Le Marois prize at Deauville
articles.summary: Ahead of a busy weekend of action domestically and on the continent, the Weekend Winners trio of Kate Tracey, Declan Rix and Sam Boswell return to preview racing from Newbury, Ripon and Deauville; Watch the episode on the At The Races YouTube channel.
articles.body:
Despite defeat at the hands of Blue Bolt last time, Aidan O'Brien's Precise heads the betting for the Group 1 showdown for three-year-olds and over. The yard won the race with Diego Velazquez last term and will be confident of another success here, with Ryan Moore booked to ride.

The British contingent are represented by Zeus Olympios and More Thunder, whilst Sixpence and Strauss fly the flag for Japan. In terms of the home side, Rayif holds strong claims for Francis-Henri Graffard after victory in the French 2000 Guineas earlier in the season.

"I'm liking the Francis Henri Graffard-trained Rayif , who will be happier back at a mile than last time [when fifth in the Prix Jean Prat over seven furlongs]. He won the French 2000 Guineas impressively with cut under foot and if he bounces back, on that run he will be a dangerous challenger.

"The drop to seven behind Thesecretadversary was a good run, given he had a setback going into Royal Ascot. He wasn't ideally placed in the race and ran on well and I think there is plenty of pace on offer here. He can sit and stalk the leaders and is overpriced against the older horses here.

"I am with Rayif as well here. I'm hoping he can bounce back to his French 2000 Guineas form. Last time it all went wrong - he was down in trip and in the wrong position. I am hoping he can build on that.

"This is the first race he has had this season in which he has had this target, without any interruptions this time. The surface is quick - which is the opposite of his Guineas win - but connections have said they are wanting better ground so this should be in his favour."

"I thought Precise was interesting in here. She has been a typical Aidan O'Brien three-year-old filly who is battle-hardened and was campaigned strongly this year. We saw her run at Deauville behind Blue Bolt in the Prix Rothschild, which she ran creditably in.

"My only concern is the quick turnarounds repeatedly, which it is for her even though she has shown she is good enough to compete at this level. I think she could get the Group One against the boys here."

articles.title: Dutch GP 2026 Sprint weekend dates, schedule, weather, UK start time and how to watch or stream F1 race at Zandvoort live on Sky Sports
articles.summary: Find out the race-day schedule, weather and how to watch the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint weekend at Zandvoort; watch the Dutch Grand Prix on Sunday at 2pm (build-up from 12.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
This is also the last Dutch Grand Prix as the event has not been renewed beyond this year, so the Orange Army will be out to support Max Verstappen racing on home soil for potentially the final time in his career.

Verstappen is yet to win a race this year but could play a key role in the title race as Kimi Antonelli looks to remain in control of the Drivers' Championship.

Antonelli leads Lewis Hamilton by 50 points and George Russell by 59 points but that advantage could quickly disappear, particularly if Ferrari continue to bring upgrades.

On paper, the Zandvoort circuit should suit Ferrari as it does not feature many straights but McLaren's Lando Norris won last time out at the twisty Hungaroring and should also be a threat.

Oscar Piastri won last year's Dutch Grand Prix, which is currently his last victory in F1, and the Australian needs to rediscover that form again in the second half of this season.

It is also a big race for Russell, who got engaged to his long-term partner Carmen Montero Mundt over the summer break, given Antonelli's superb recent form.

Dutch GP circuit: Zandvoort track layout

Zandvoort is one of the drivers' favourite tracks thanks to its high-speed corners and banked bends at Turn 3 and the flat-out final turn.

It can be tricky to overtake with only one long straight down to Turn 1 so track position is critical and we could see a similar race to Hungary last time out.

articles.title: Crouch guides Coppull home in Hungerford to complete big-race double
articles.summary: Coppull completed a valuable double for Hector Crouch and the Clive Cox team at Newbury on Saturday with a dominant display in the Group Two Hungerford Stakes
articles.body:
The three-year-old Clive Cox-trained colt finished third in the July Cup last time out but a bold plan to move up to seven furlongs was landed in fine style for his jockey, who also completing a treble on the card.

Crouch delivered Coppull in eyecatching style, too, peeling away from the main group towards the far side two-and-a-half furlongs from home at the head of a three-strong breakaway, a path which proved quicker to the line.

It proved a masterstroke as the Bated Breath colt stayed on too strongly to land the £93,571 pot by one-and-a-quarter lengths at 15-2 from Prince Of India (14-1) with a further three-quarters of a length back to another of the breakaway trio, the 5-2 favourite Symbol Of Honour.

Cox, who was credited by Crouch with the decision to go far side, said victory over seven furlongs had given them options for the remainder of the season.

"He was unlucky not to be a place closer at least in the July Cup but he always gave me the impression he would stretch another furlong, even as a two-year-old where he ran so well in the Coventry," he told ITV Racing .

"He's got a lot of class and he reminds me an awful lot of Lethal Force who won this race back in 2012 and he went on to be champion sprinter the year after he won this.

"He's still quick enough for six furlongs and while I'm not convinced he likes it really soft, with the dry summer we've had we've got choices now.

"If he comes back all right we could still run in the Haydock Sprint Cup and that would be with a bit of confidence after today. And we still have the Park Stakes [Group Two over seven furlongs at Doncaster] which obviously he would have a penalty in."

Melbourne Cup next stop for Wine Dark Sea after Freer success

Wine Dark Sea made every yard of the running to land a gamble in the Highclere Thoroughbred Racing Geoffrey Freer Stakes at Newbury and set up a possible tilt at the Melbourne Cup.

Connections have recently sold a share in the four-year-old gelding to Australian Bloodstock and victory under Hector Crouch was enough to earn a place in the Flemington race.

Making all under Crouch, Wine Dark Sea, who was well backed from 13-2 into 7-2, never looked like being pegged back and stayed on well in the straight to pull clear of the staying-on Tabletalk to win by a length and a half.

William Haggas' 2-1 favourite Dubai Honour was a neck further back in third.

Winning trainer Harry Charlton confirmed the Melbourne spectacular was the next stop for the improving four-year-old with the horse set to go into quarantine on September 9.

"The intention today was to finish third which would help with the ballot qualification for the Melbourne Cup and he has done more than that," said Charlton.

"The Aussies who I'm dealing with were saying finish third and they won't change his handicap mark. It is very different how they do it."

Wine Dark Sea ran out an impressive winner of handicaps at Ascot and Carlisle earlier in the season but could manage only fifth when well supported at Newmarket's July meeting.

Charlton was inclined to put that disappointment down to the rigours of a stiff finish and long journey to the Cumbrian track.

"Although he won on the bridle at Carlisle he broke the track record carrying top weight so you can't have an easy race, particularly travelling eight hours in a heatwave. The 10 days later we just saw a slightly flat horse.

"My brother [Tom] trains in Australia and has a Melbourne Cup runner as well. I have a team going down with the horse and you train out of the quarantine barn at Ballarat."

articles.title: Godolphin's Gold Cup hero Trawlerman retired
articles.summary: John Gosden announced the news that Godolphin's staying star Trawlerman has been forced into retirement on Saturday, having picked up a leg issue after his run in the Goodwood Cup.
articles.body:
The eight-year-old, who won over £2m in prize-money, also won the Long Distance Cup on Champions Day twice and an Ebor.

Trained by John and Thady Gosden, he returned from an eight-month lay off to run a tremendous race in this year's Gold Cup, pushing his much younger rival Scandinavia all the way before succumbing by just a head.

He took on that same rival again but in an unsatisfactory race where he was hampered by a loose horse, he was beaten a long way.

Just this year the Gosdens realised he had a condition in his eyes that made them very sensitive to sunlight and he has been wearing ski goggles to protect them from the sun.

"Trawlerman is happy and well, but unfortunately he came out of the Goodwood Cup with a leg issue and is now being retired," John Gosden told

"At eight years old, he has become part of the family here and won the Long Distance Cup twice and the Ascot Gold Cup in a very fast record time, which is unlikely to be equalled, as well as the Ebor.

"He has won over £2m in prize-money and remained at the top of his game this year when second in the Ascot Gold Cup, beaten a head giving 1lb to the winner.

"He will be retired to Wood Ditton Stud, where Godolphin have wonderful facilities that he knows well having been there for holiday.

"For all of us at Clarehaven Stables, just like Stradivarius, Trawlerman has become a much-loved member of the family and there are a lot of people here who will miss him particularly Ben de Paiva, who looks after him and Richard Wilkinson, who rode him through most of his career."

articles.title: Deauville: Rayif roars back to his best to land Prix Jacques le Marois
articles.summary: Francis-Henri Graffard added yet another Group 1 crown to his collection when French 2000 Guineas winner Rayif battled to victory in the Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques Le Marois at Deauville.
articles.body:
Francis-Henri Graffard's colt struck Classic gold on what was his seasonal debut in the Poule d'Essai des Poulains in early May, but his summer campaign has been interrupted, with a planned visit to Royal Ascot scuppered by a minor setback after which he ran a little below par when fifth in the Prix Jean Prat.

He had plenty on his plate stepping back up to a mile, with Aidan O'Brien's Irish 1,000 Guineas and Coronation Stakes winner Precise the hot favourite after bumping into top-class older filly Blue Bolt on her last couple of starts.

Fozzy Stack's Prix Jean Prat victor Thesecretadversary took the field along for much of the way, closely pursued by Karl Burke's Zeus Olympios, who looked the likely winner after quickening to the lead inside the final furlong.

But Mickael Barzalona delivered Rayif with a withering late run and he got up to deny Zeus Olympios an elusive first Group One success, with Precise close up behind in third.

"I'm very happy, it's a wonderful race to win, a very hard race to win," said Graffard.

"I kept my confidence in the horse. He ran pretty well the other day with excuses and he was in top form (today). Over that course you need the perfect trip and we had the perfect trip today.

"He travelled really well and picked up really nicely, he's very tough and game.

"He won the Poule d'Essai on very soft ground so everyone was saying he's a soft ground horse, but you need to keep trying and if these horses are to find their place at stud they need to be performing at this level.

"The Jacques le Marois is a very famous race - probably the second most famous race in France after the Arc - so it's a wonderful race to win. It means so much."

Rayif has a range of options for the second half of the season, including the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes at Ascot on Champions Day, for which he was cut to 4-1 second-favourite from 14-1 by Coral.

Graffard added: "It depends if we decide to go for the Prix du Moulin (September 6) or give him more time and the Prix de la Foret (October 4) could be an option - I wouldn't be afraid to drop him back in distance.

"There is the QEII at the back-end and we know he can handle soft ground."

Of the gallant runner-up, Burke said: "We always thought and hoped he would produce that sort of performance in a Group One. I think physically he's improving and he showed that today.

"He quickened twice there - first time I thought we'd got it, then he got challenged and then he quickened again and I thought we'd got it and so did Cliff (Lee, jockey).

"The winner, fair play to him, has come and cut us down. Francis can do no wrong, can he?

"We'll get him home and see how he is. It's got to be discussed, but as a trainer I'm very hopeful he'll stay in training next year and I think he'll just continue improving physically and strengthening, so hopefully if he doesn't win his Group One this year he'll certainly get it next year.

"I'd say the race at Longchamp (Moulin) will probably come a bit quick for him, maybe we'll wait for the QEII at Ascot."
